text:
olivia: Pager - alerting: sustained GPU pool throttle > 90% for 6m, queue depth jump on us-east-1-gpu-1. Observed token rate falling and lots of prefix-cache misses in logs. Anyone oncall?

pagerbot: [ALERT] PAGER: GPU_POOL_THROTTLE (sev2) triggered by autoscaler. Page to oncall. Incident ID: INC-2026-1928473.

samir: I'm on it, grabbing logs. First glance shows autoscaler attempted scale but a quota-controller returned 429/LimitExceeded and autoscaler entered backoff. Queue kept growing.

marta: any config changes pushed recently to batching/caching?

olivia: We shipped a continuous-batching param change 45m ago that shrinks batching window when latency spikes (cc @ken). Also a prefix-cache TTL change rolled earlier today (ttl from 300->30s) for dev testing, but I thought that was gated.

ken: I pushed the TTL change in infra-dev yesterday and it somehow made it into prod via a config staging promotion. Noticed high miss rates but didn't think it would hit this hard. Reverting now.

samir: Logs snippet from the router:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z WARN prefix-cache miss key=mdl:v1:prompthash:abc123
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR batcher: flush_timeout=20ms queued=172 pool=us-east-1-gpu-1
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z INFO autoscaler: scale_attempt=3 reason=quota_controller:LimitExceeded
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z WARN gpu-driver: allocation failed: insufficient capacity
```

samir: We're seeing continuous-batching window shrink + cache TTL drop => much fewer prefix cache hits -> more token work -> GPU utilization increased -> autoscaler tried to add pods but quota blocked.

olivia: Impact: API 5xx rate went from ~0.2% to 6% for hosted customers using gpt-az-*-prod models in us-east. Affected top-tier customer 'SequoiaMail' reported degraded latency and dropped responses. Support notified.

support-anne: Support ticket #CS-6792 created for SequoiaMail, they reported ~30% of requests getting partial responses. I've added the customer impact note and escalation.

marta: Can we do emergency mitigation: 1) revert prefix-cache TTL in config store, 2) temporarily increase autoscaler upper bound (if quota allows), 3) put burst policy to use smaller model variant fallback.

ken: Reverting TTL now. Command:
```
redwood-config set /prod/serving/prefix_cache/ttl 300 --author=ken --reason="revert accidental promo"
```

ken: Revert applied. TTL showing 300s in prod. Monitoring cache-hit ratio.

samir: While TTL rolled, autoscaler still in backoff due to quota error. I increased autoscaler retry and forced a scale attempt (bypassing soft backoff) but it immediately returned LimitExceeded. We need headroom from cloud quota or reduce demand.

olivia: Can we temporarily change routing to favor small-model fallback for noisy customers? I can add a rule to route non-SLA customers to model-lite-1 for 10m.

marta: Do it. Add a canary route that matches customer tag != enterprise. Command:
```
redwood-route update /routes/fallbacks add --match="customer.tier!=enterprise" --model=model-lite-1 --duration=10m
```

olivia: Rule live. About 18% of traffic offloaded to lite model. Latency improves for critical requests.

samir: Cache-hit ratio climbing after TTL revert: was 6% -> now 64% within 2m. Pool token work dropped ~55%. Good. Autoscaler still required cloud quota bump though.

pagerbot: [STATUS] INC-2026-1928473 assigned to samir (oncall). State: mitigation in progress.

ken: Filing quota request with cloud: submitted increase for GPU quota in us-east-1 from 200->260. Request ID CLD-99821. ETA 25m.

olivia: Short-term perf: we've lowered continuous-batching shrink aggressiveness to previous value. Patch applied:
```
batch.window.shrink_factor = 0.8 -> 0.95
```
Applied via hot config. Confirmed no regressions in canary.

samir: Observed GPU pool utilization drop from 98% -> 75% after config changes + routing offload. Queue depth trending down. No new 5xx spikes in last 5m.

support-anne: Notified SequoiaMail with ETA 45m for full resolution and temporary mitigation steps. They requested a postmortem and timeline.

marta: Preparing timeline for incident. Key events so far: 14:02 root alert, 14:04 TTL accidental promo surfaced, 14:07 revert applied, 14:11 routing offload, 14:18 autoscaler still limited by cloud quota, 14:22 cloud quota request submitted.

olivia: Handoff: my shift ends in 20m. @oncall-next please take over monitoring and coordinate with cloud support for quota. Documented actions in incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-1928473 (private).

oncall-next: Acked. I'll monitor for 2h and escalate to infra team if quota not approved. Also will check that revert fully rolled to all regions.

samir: Quick follow-up: we uncovered an unsafe config promotion path where infra-dev flags could leak into prod via a one-step config merge. I'll open a PR to add gating and a preflight check for prefix-cache TTL changes.

ken: Agree. Also adding a runtime guard that prevents TTL < 60s in prod. PR linked: https://git.redwood/repo/infra-config/pull/824

pagerbot: [RESOLVE PROGRESS] Cache hit rate recovered, queue < threshold, RPS stabilized. Keep monitoring.

olivia: Next steps: 1) Follow up with cloud about quota bump, 2) postmortem to describe config promotion bug + hardening + customer comms, 3) schedule a small retro to tighten preflight.

support-anne: Raising CS-6792 to high priority and drafting customer post-incident note.

oncall-next: Taking over. If quota not granted in 30m, will trigger reserve capacity fallback (dedicated spare pool) to avoid customer exposure.

samir: Will leave active logs/metrics links in the incident doc and hand over runbooks.

olivia: Thanks team. Marking this thread for follow-up; will sync on postmortem tomorrow at 10:00. :thumbsup:
